Oct 29 : Indian fintech firm Pine Labs reported a more than sixfold jump in second-quarter profit on Thursday, buoyed by rising adoption of digital payment services, sending its shares up nearly 6 per cent. More than 500 million people use the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) in India for transactions ranging from everyday purchases to high-value consumer goods. Here are some details: • Consolidated profit rose to 385.7 million rupees ($4.05 million) in the quarter ended September, up from 59.7 million rupees a year earlier

Oct 29 : Nasdaq futures dropped on Thursday as mixed earnings from Alphabet and Microsoft left investors weighing the payoff from heavy AI spending, with focus also on an inflation reading a day after the Federal Reserve left interest rates unchanged. Alphabet slid 10.5 per cent in premarket trading after the company reported disappointing results in the core business of search advertising and a massive acceleration in cash burn as it poured resources into building out AI. "Investors are starting to scrutinize monetization timelines versus the capital expenditure burn rates. Some investors are no longer giving all hyperscalers a 'free pass' to spend without limit," said Jeremy Saltzberg, VP and senior investment officer at Check Capital Management. On the other hand, Microsoft climbed 3.5 per cent after the company delivered a big cash-flow beat and forecast strong cloud growth, offering fresh evidence that its hefty AI bets were working.

Other early movers included cybersecurity firm Fortinet, which tumbled 25.4 per cent after reporting third-quarter results. Software maker ServiceNow dropped 19 per cent after missing third-quarter profit estimates. Other software-related companies, including Zscaler and Salesforce, were among the laggards in sector-wide weakness. Marvell Technology fell 9.4 per cent after media reports said the company is in advanced talks to buy data-center optics maker Lumentum Holdings. Lumentum shares rose 4.3 per cent. Marvell and Lumentum did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment. The broader semiconductor space was trading lower, with Nvidia down 1 per cent, AMD sliding 3.3 per cent and Intel off 3.6 per cent. Intel and Amazon are some of the major tech companies reporting after markets close on Thursday. On the earnings docket before the bell are drugmakers Merck and Eli Lilly, construction equipment maker Caterpillar, and alternative investment managers Ares Management and Blue Owl. At 4:09 a.m. ET, Dow E-minis were up 185 points, or 0.35 per cent, and S&P 500 E-minis were down 31 points, or 0.41 per cent. Nasdaq 100 E-minis were down 365 points, or 1.22 per cent. Meanwhile, the Federal Reserve held interest rates steady on Wednesday, as expected, opting to delay any changes to borrowing costs until after next week's US midterm elections while it awaits further data on inflation. "The decision to hold seems to be a short pause to assess ahead of a likely policy hike in December, rather than an indication that no further tightening is needed," said Jon Butcher, a senior US economist at Aberdeen. Focus will be on the September Personal Consumption Expenditures report, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, due later in the day. A third-quarter GDP reading is also set for release. Traders currently see a more than 81 per cent chance the Fed will hike interest rates in December, as per the CME FedWatch Tool, as key inflation metrics remain elevated amid the oil shock caused by the Middle East conflict. Money market participants are also pricing an additional rate hike by mid-2027, according to data compiled by LSEG. Among other stocks, car e-commerce platform Carvana jumped 9.2 per cent after its third-quarter revenue surpassed estimates, while Chipotle Mexican Grill gained 6.7 per cent after reporting better-than-expected quarterly comparable sales.

Source: Reuters

Oct 29 : STMicroelectronics reported a third-quarter operating profit above market expectations on Thursday, as demand from AI data centres and satellite operators added to a broader recovery in the chipmaker's markets. Operating income excluding one-off charges was $429 million, nearly doubling from a year ago and beating the $400.5 million expected by analysts polled by LSEG. The Franco-Italian chipmaker said it expected fourth-quarter revenue of $4.15 billion, up from $3.76 billion in the third quarter, give or take 3.5 per cent. Analysts polled by LSEG had expected $4.10 billion. "In an environment where demand remains well above supply, we continue to expand capacity aligned with ST's strategic roadmap," CEO Jean-Marc Chery said in the earnings statement.

STMicro, which makes chips ranging from microcontrollers to sensors and power semiconductors for cars, factories and smartphones, said higher sales of communication equipment, computer peripherals and personal electronics drove the beat. It had said already in July that fourth-quarter sales would be more than $4 billion. Chery said on Thursday that company-specific drivers, including AI data centre demand and low-Earth-orbit satellite communications, were adding to the cyclical recovery. The company's gross margin rose to 37.3 per cent in the third quarter from 33.2 per cent a year ago, helped by a higher share of sales from more profitable chips and lower costs from idle factory capacity. STMicro expects the margin to rise to about 39 per cent in the fourth quarter. Jefferies analysts expect STMicro's growth to continue into 2027, as data centre revenue is set to roughly double from this year to the next, while gross margins see "more significant upside towards the end of next year", they wrote in an early take on the report.

TOKYO, Oct 29 : Japanese government bonds (JGBs) were steady on Thursday, a day before the Bank of Japan's monetary policy decision, while strong demand at an auction of 2-year notes provided support. The market was also buoyed by gains in US Treasuries after the Federal Reserve left interest rates unchanged and gave few signals about the chances of a hike at the next meeting in December. "The market seemed to perceive it as less hawkish than expected," said Yuhi Kawano, a market analyst at Mizuho Securities. "Under these circumstances, it’s easy to see why the need for the Bank of Japan to raise rates at a high pace seems low, which should be supportive for the yen bond market."

SEOUL, Oct 29 : South Korea's export growth likely accelerated to its fastest pace in more than 50 years in October, a Reuters poll showed on Thursday, driven by robust demand for AI investment-related semiconductors and higher memory chip prices. Exports from Asia's fourth-largest economy, a bellwether for global trade, were forecast to have risen 93.2 per cent this month from a year earlier, up from an 83.7 per cent increase in September, the median estimate of nine economists surveyed by Reuters showed. If realised, it would mark a 17th straight month of export growth and the strongest increase since January 1974. South Korea's exports exceeded $800 billion in the first nine months of the year, already surpassing last year's full-year record. The AI-driven chip boom has continued to fuel the economy. South Korea's gross domestic product grew 1.0 per cent in the third quarter, beating expectations, while chip manufacturer SK Hynix reported a more than seven-fold jump in quarterly profit.

Economists attributed the export growth to robust semiconductor demand tied to AI investment and firmer memory chip prices, but cautioned that calendar effects played a significant role. October had 22 working days compared with 20 a year earlier, owing to differences in the timing of Chuseok holidays, which often distort South Korea's trade data in September and October. "The likely sharp increases in exports and imports mainly reflect calendar effects and favourable base comparisons rather than a comparable acceleration in underlying trade activity," said Park Chong-hoon, an economist at Standard Chartered.   Stephen Lee, an analyst at Meritz Securities, said exports were driven by semiconductors and computers on AI investment demand, while growth momentum was also broadening to other sectors such as cars and wireless communication devices. "Higher volumes, not just higher export prices, are clearly contributing to GDP growth," Lee said.  Imports were forecast to have risen 39.9 per cent in October from a year earlier, accelerating from a 26.0 per cent gain in September and marking the strongest increase since November 2021. The monthly trade surplus was forecast at a median $37.24 billion, down from September's $49.97 billion surplus. South Korea is scheduled to report October trade figures on Sunday, November 1, at 9 a.m. (0000 GMT).

Source: Reuters

SEOUL, Oct 29 : A voting member on the Bank of Korea's board warned that the recent pace of the won's moves warranted close monitoring, signalling caution over the currency even as the export-reliant economy benefits from booming demand for AI chips. "With the exchange rate, you have to look at volatility and the speed of its moves rather than the level," Hwang Kunil said in an interview with Reuters. "The pace of the recent move has been somewhat faster than expected. We are watching volatility closely." "That said, once the massive current account surplus and foreign investment rebalancing are adjusted, downward pressure on the exchange rate remains valid." Hwang, a former deputy finance minister and World Bank executive director, said the won's recent gains came as surging dollar inflows from the global artificial intelligence buildout fuelled demand for specialised memory chips from top Korean chipmakers SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics.

Hwang is viewed by analysts as one of the most dovish members of the central bank's seven-member board. He opposed August's quarter-point hike in interest rates, which highlighted a debate over how far tightening should go. This is his first interview since joining the board in February 2024, marking the first time he has detailed monetary policy trade-offs amid Asia’s fourth-largest economy's massive current account surplus. A veteran financial diplomat for South Korea, Hwang managed the country's currency policy during US President Donald Trump's first term, navigating intense pressure when Washington accused Seoul of engineering excessive current-account surpluses. The BOK held interest rates steady at 3.00 per cent this month following back-to-back hikes in July and August, but left further tightening on the table amid inflation risks due to energy prices and a resilient economic recovery. The won gained about 13 per cent against the greenback in the third quarter, logging the sharpest rise in value since the fourth quarter of 1998. While a strong currency traditionally buffers import costs, Hwang noted that exports remain the bedrock of the country's macroeconomic structure. "It's not what it used to be, but exports are still the backbone of our economic structure," he said. UNEQUAL GROWTH On the domestic price outlook, Hwang projected that headline consumer price inflation would start approaching the central bank’s 2.0 per cent target towards the end of the first half of 2027. He expects inflation to be fully stabilised at the target by the end of next year or early 2028. "What we need to focus on right now is, of course, the trajectory of inflation," Hwang said. While he expects blistering export momentum to continue for the time being, he expressed concern that the positive economic impact has not been distributed evenly. Private consumption was recovering at a slower pace, while small and medium-sized companies continued to deal with elevated delinquency rates and weak domestic demand, he said. "The positives are limited to certain groups, while high rates and prices affect everyone," he said. "It depends on which side proves to be stronger." Hwang also expressed caution about the underlying quality of corporate financing for smaller businesses. Their delinquency rates were climbing, while much of their borrowing was going to cover immediate operating costs, such as wages and raw materials, rather than expanding capital investments. Asked whether a slowdown in global AI spending could hurt export-led growth, Hwang said this year's current-account surplus could be revised up to nearly $500 billion from the BOK's August forecast of $450 billion. A shortfall amounting to about a tenth of that, or $50 billion, would "of course" be a blow, he said, citing an earlier BOK projection on the potential implications of a slowdown. "But this boom is likely to last somewhat longer," he said.

Source: Reuters

FAST

SYDNEY: Asian shares gave up earlier gains on Thursday (Oct 29) as AI-related earnings announcements prompted wildly mixed responses, raising the stakes for Amazon and Intel results due later in the day. Hefty cash burn from Alphabet sent its shares 10 per cent lower in after-hours trading, wiping nearly US$400 billion off its market value. That drove Nasdaq futures 1 per cent lower. Microsoft, by contrast, beat forecasts with better-than-expected cash flows that lifted its shares by 3 per cent. Overnight, the Federal Reserve held interest rates steady as widely expected , but two committee members voted for a hike. Chair Kevin Warsh struck a more confident note on the inflation outlook during his press conference, sparking a rally in Treasuries. However, the bigger test came from earnings. Samsung Electronics said on Thursday its operating profit rose nearly ninefold to a record high in the third quarter, driven by robust demand for AI chips. Its shares still slid more than 4 per cent and dragged the broader KOSPI index down 2.6 per cent after a nearly 7 per cent surge a day earlier.

MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan dropped 0.7 per cent, while Japan's Nikkei trimmed gains to be up 0.3 per cent. Mainland China's blue chips fell 0.9 per cent and Hong Kong's Hang Seng index rose 0.2 per cent. "The reason why Alphabet is down is because their traditional revenue service of ad generation has been impacted by the very thing which is the AI boom. So it's causing a mix of results for Google," said Jamie Hannah, deputy head of investments at VanEck. "Both of Alphabet and Microsoft confirmed that the AI revenue generation is still solid. We saw that through the data center growth, the cloud services. So that part of the business is solid, which then flows into a lot of the information coming out of Asia with SK Hynix yesterday as well in Korea." Shares of SK Hynix rose 1.3 per cent after jumping 11 per cent a day earlier on strong earnings. CENTRAL BANK FEST CONTINUES After the Fed held interest rates steady, all eyes are on US Personal Consumption Expenditures data for September, the Fed's preferred gauge of inflation. Forecasts are centred on a 0.3 per cent monthly rise in the core measure, picking up from a 0.2 per cent gain the previous month. Markets are still 80 per cent priced for a rate rise in December despite dovish comments from Warsh, which led to a steepening of the Treasury yield curve. The 2-year Treasury yield fell 6 basis points overnight and was last flat at 4.6933 per cent. "The dissenting votes to hike rates at today’s meeting could be interpreted as being not about whether the Fed hikes again, but when," said Kerry Craig, global market strategist at JP Morgan Asset Management. "With policy tightening already being priced in, this implies that yields will remain range-bound unless there is a clearer signal for more aggressive policy tightening or a pivot to cuts," he said. The Bank of Canada hiked interest rates on Wednesday for the first time in more than three years and warned of further increases. The European Central Bank is, however, expected to hold interest rates steady later on Thursday. In the currency markets, the dollar was steady against its major peers after a 0.2 per cent dip overnight. The kiwi was nursing heavy losses at US$0.5626, having slid 1 per cent overnight as its central bank shocked markets by leaving interest rates steady on Wednesday. Brent crude futures fell 0.4 per cent on Thursday to US$114.91 a barrel after the Wall Street Journal reported US Vice President JD Vance sent a letter to Iranian Security Council chief Mohsen Rezaei in an effort to revive peace negotiations.

HONG KONG, Oct 29 : The Hong Kong Monetary Authority left its base interest rate unchanged on Thursday at 4.25 per cent, following the US Federal Reserve's decision to hold rates steady. Hong Kong's monetary policy moves in lock-step with the United States as the city's currency is pegged to the greenback in a tight range of 7.75-7.85 per dollar. The Hong Kong dollar was last at 7.8452 per dollar. "US interest rate adjustments are subject to considerable uncertainty, and will depend on developments in inflation, labour market, and other economic data, and may influence the interest rate environment in Hong Kong," HKMA said in a statement. The outlook for the Hong Kong dollar and interbank rates can vary due to various factors, such as the market's risk appetite for carry trades, and the supply-demand conditions for Hong Kong dollars which are, in turn, influenced by capital market activities and other seasonal factors, it added.

HANOI, Oct 29 : Vietnam has approved a plan to set the minimum state ownership level for state-run lenders at 65 per cent by 2030, part of a broader programme to restructure state capital in major enterprises and banks. The restructuring plan, released late on Wednesday, covers 21 state-owned and state-backed enterprises, and forms part of Vietnam's 2026-2030 programme to restructure state capital, with the aim of preserving state control in strategic sectors while giving authorities the flexibility to adjust their holdings in selected companies and lenders. • The state plans to retain shares of at least 65 per cent in BIDV, Vietcombank and VietinBank by 2030. FAST

Oct 29 : Cash flow is king again. Wall Street rewarded Microsoft and Oracle on Wednesday for showing that they could fund their enormous AI ambitions without endlessly tapping investors. Alphabet, by contrast, was punished for burning through cash, while Google Search's slower growth fanned fears that competition was hurting the business that bankrolls its AI expansion. Microsoft shares jumped more than 3 per cent in after-hours trading, while Alphabet plunged nearly 10 per cent, as investors drew a sharper distinction between companies making money from AI and those struggling to contain its costs.

The divergence shows that after rewarding companies for spending aggressively to secure computing capacity — often through debt — investors are demanding more evidence that the resulting growth can finance the next round of outlays. Meta offered an early warning last week, when better-than-expected revenue growth and an upbeat outlook were eclipsed by its cash burn. Oracle, on the other hand, ended regular trading nearly 11 per cent higher on Wednesday after Larry Ellison's company said it was planning to put a ceiling on external financing and expected to turn its cash flow positive in the second half of fiscal 2028. "Alphabet and Microsoft were night and day," said Melissa Otto, head of research at S&P Global Visible Alpha. "Microsoft's quarter demonstrated very disciplined growth, whereas Google is burning cash and its core business came in below expectations," she said, adding that it may lead investors to question "is AI taking some share" from Google Search. Google's search revenue grew 12 per cent in the September quarter but fell short of expectations for a 14.7 per cent increase, even as CEO Sundar Pichai said queries were growing at their fastest pace in five years. The long-lucrative business is under threat from AI chatbots and agents that are changing how people search for information, just as the company pours more money into the technology. Capital expenditure will increase significantly in 2027, CFO Anat Ashkenazi told analysts. CLOUD BOOM, CASH SQUEEZE Alphabet's eyebrow-raising capital outlay — with as much as $205 billion expected this year — is, however, driving gains at Google's other major AI business. Google Cloud revenue more than doubled to $30.71 billion, but Alphabet's spending overwhelmed that growth. Cash burn hit $9.07 billion after the company posted its first quarter of negative cash flow in the June period. "This is definitely a different business, Google. It's a different business today than it was three, five, 10 years ago," said Jeremy Saltzberg, vice president and senior investment officer at Check Capital, which owns Alphabet shares. Saltzberg pushed back on the concerns about spending, saying Alphabet needed to have big outlays to stay competitive at a time when OpenAI and Anthropic appear to be pulling ahead in Silicon Valley's AI model race. "We think this is a sport of kings, which is that if you don't have $150 billion to spend next year on capital expenditure, don't even bother showing up," Saltzberg said. MICROSOFT'S CASH FLOW ADVANTAGE Microsoft offered a stark contrast. The company generated $18.6 billion in free cash flow in its fiscal first quarter, nearly $10 billion more than Wall Street expected, even as it poured $45.2 billion into expanding its computing infrastructure. Revenue at its Azure cloud business surged a better-than-expected 48 per cent and the company forecast faster-than-expected cloud growth for the current quarter, suggesting corporate demand for AI computing remains strong. The results also suggested Microsoft was finding a broader market for AI beyond a handful of deep-pocketed customers, including OpenAI, whose heavy computing requirements have fueled the industry's expansion. "The shiny object stuff is waning" as more businesses move beyond experimenting with the newest or most powerful AI models and commit to long-term contracts, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said in a conference call with analysts. "I want the breadth," he said. "We have large customers who want to buy from us ... As long as the pricing is right, we may sell them some. If not, we will be patient about building the breadth business."

Source: Reuters

SEOUL, Oct 29 : A South Korean court on Thursday rejected a lawsuit by dozens of Tesla owners seeking full refunds for money paid for "Full Self-Driving" driver-assistance software, ruling that the automaker had not breached its contractual obligations. The Seoul Central District Court ruled against the 88 plaintiffs, finding that the FSD option did not promise fully autonomous driving without human intervention and that Tesla had already provided some of the functions included in the package. The court said Tesla's obligation to deliver additional features depended on technological advances and regulatory approvals, adding that buyers had been aware that some functions could take considerable time to become available. It also found that Tesla had provided basic Autopilot and Enhanced Autopilot functions, while a recent software update had added traffic light and sign recognition, as well as city-driving capabilities, to older vehicles equipped with Hardware 3 (HW3) computers.

SYDNEY, Oct 29 : Australia's corporate regulator said on Thursday it was probing the failed $5 billion initial public offering of AI data centre operator Firmus. Firmus' planned IPO, due to be the second-largest ever in Australia, collapsed on October 9 after failing to gain enough backing amid mounting investor concerns over AI valuations, heavy spending and the timing of returns, tempering the optimism that fuelled the sector's rapid rise. Australian Securities and Investments Commission Chair Sarah Court said the regulator was yet to launch an official investigation, but said it had engaged with the banks leading the share sale. The deal's joint lead managers were Bank of America, JPMorgan, Morgan Stanley and brokerage Morgans.

Bank of America, Morgan Stanley and JPMorgan declined to comment on the ASIC inquiries, while Morgans did not respond to a Reuters request for comment. "I think it's fair to say that we are having a look at the broad range of issues that have been reported in the media, including engaging with the joint lead managers," Court told a hearing of Australian lawmakers. "This was a very significant event. We understand that and we need to look at it carefully. That's what we're doing."  Some investors have criticised as misleading a term sheet sent by the banks when the deal and pricing were launched on October 1 that said "at this fixed price indications are in excess of the offer size."  A broker at one of the firms, Morgans, also sent an email to clients that said Firmus' order book was well above the deal's size, according to local media reports, suggesting strong demand. Court said messaging from brokers during the IPO's bookbuild would form part of ASIC's inquiry into the failed deal. In a separate letter responding to questions raised by Liberal Senator Dave Sharma, Court said ASIC had standards that banks were expected to meet during capital raisings. "We expect lead managers to have a reasonable basis for representations about investor demand, keep appropriate records of bookbuild and allocation decisions, manage conflicts of interest, and update investors if demand changes materially during the capital-raising process," Court wrote in the letter dated Wednesday and seen by Reuters. ASIC declined to comment beyond the contents of the letter. Nvidia-backed Firmus had planned to raise $5 billion in the IPO to value the company at $30.6 billion, triple the value achieved during a private fundraising round in August. The deal's collapse added to a wave of negative sentiment towards AI stocks, which had driven global equity gains for much of the past two years, and stoked fears the sector's fundraising ability could start to ease.

SEOUL: Samsung Electronics said on Thursday (Oct 29) it expects an AI-driven memory chip shortage to deepen next year, after posting nearly a ninefold jump in quarterly profit on robust demand for AI chips. But a lack of fresh details from the world's top memory chipmaker on plans to return its AI windfall to shareholders, along with chip earnings falling slightly short of lofty expectations, disappointed investors, sending its shares down more than 6 per cent. Shareholders' hopes were up as Samsung's cross-town rival SK Hynix on Wednesday reported better-than-expected earnings and spelled out plans to return about US$75 billion to shareholders this year. "SK Hynix did quite a lot more than expected yesterday ... it went beyond market expectations, but Samsung Electronics hasn't really changed anything from the guidance it gave before," said Lee Min-hee, analyst at BNK Investment & Securities.

Samsung, however, echoed SK Hynix's upbeat outlook, helping to ease market concerns that AI-driven chip earnings could lose momentum. "In 2027, the (memory) business expects AI infrastructure capital expenditure to reach a historic level as the AI ecosystem expands," it said in a statement. "Increasing AI-driven demand will far exceed the industry supply in comparison with 2026." Samsung reported operating profit of 107.4 trillion won (US$80.04 billion) for the July-to-September period, in line with its estimate and up from 12.2 trillion won a year earlier. Its semiconductor division posted a 15-fold jump in the third quarter from a year earlier to 106.5 trillion won, accounting for almost all of the group's total profit, but that was short of analysts' estimate of 107.3 trillion won, according to LSEG. Samsung shares opened higher but reversed course, falling as much as 6.2 per cent in morning trade, while SK Hynix rose 0.7 per cent. The company previously said this year's shareholder returns would total between 90 trillion and 110 trillion won including 30 trillion won in third-quarter dividends. On Thursday, it said it would finalise its next shareholder return policy in January. HIGHER CHIP CAPEX Capital spending in Samsung's chip division will jump 62 per cent to 76.8 trillion won this year and will rise sharply next year, the company said, as it seeks to address the supply shortage. While demand for AI chips is expected to remain resilient, concerns about financing for AI infrastructure and rising competition from China have weighed on chip stocks in recent months. Google parent Alphabet reported on Wednesday a massive acceleration in cash burn as it poured resources into building out AI. The pace of memory-chip price gains is slowing as chipmakers sign more long-term supply contracts and higher chip prices weigh on demand from smartphone and personal-computer makers. The higher memory-chip costs shrank margins in Samsung's mobile business, which fell to a loss of 800 billion won.

WASHINGTON, Oct 28 : The leak website Distributed Denial of Secrets said on Wednesday it has released data on more than 40,000 Department of Homeland Security employees, including details about officials working in sensitive fields such as surveillance and human intelligence. DHS said in a statement it was "aware of a potential breach and is actively working to address the situation swiftly and effectively." The agency said it was working to ensure its employees were properly protected and would update the public "when more information is available.” The disclosure — which the nonprofit data transparency group says draws on information obtained by an entity calling itself "Department of Peace" — is the third major government data leak to have made headlines in the past month. In September, the hacking group ShinyHunters claimed the theft of a massive trove of data from the Federal Bureau of Investigation, including sensitive job details and medical information from thousands of bureau employees. Last week, the Defense Department was hit with a class action lawsuit following a breach that exposed data on millions of current and former military personnel.

The DHS data includes names, phone numbers and email addresses of employees from Immigration and Customs Enforcement, Customs and Border Protection, Homeland Security Investigations, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, and other DHS component agencies. Also included in the data were job titles and email groups, which, among other details, showed which agents were assigned to special operations, surveillance jobs, computer forensics and undercover work. In a statement, Distributed Denial of Secrets co-founder Emma Best said the hacktivist and journalist known as "maia arson crimew" developed a search tool for the data that would allow the public to browse it. Best said the tool would "replace anonymity with accountability" and empower journalists, guide public records requests and boost congressional oversight. Crimew said her tool would provide "FOIA material for years to come!" The Department of Peace did not immediately respond to a request for comment, but in a statement included with the data it said that DHS employees "have our information, so it's only fair that we have theirs" and that it hoped the data "can be used to limit further harm by the DHS and supports all efforts in that direction." The Department of Peace in March claimed responsibility for hacking DHS and posting documents related to contracts with outside vendors. Best's statement said the Department of Peace harvested the data from the Okta sign-on service used by DHS. Reuters could not immediately corroborate the claim. Okta said in response to a Reuters query: "Okta is secure, and we have no evidence our data or systems were compromised." Reuters could not immediately verify the authenticity of the entire data trove but it was able to match personal information about six DHS employees named in the leak to credit bureau records and breach data carried by the dark web intelligence platform District 4 Labs. Reuters called three DHS employees directly and was able to confirm their phone numbers and other details. One said it was the first they had heard of a breach. In several cases, the data tracked information available on DHS employees' LinkedIn profiles. But in others, the data revealed nonpublic data about internal DHS organization charts or previously undisclosed programs or operations.

Source: Reuters

Oct 29 : Oil prices fell on Thursday, paring gains made a day earlier, as hopes for peace talks took the edge off renewed concerns over Middle East supply disruptions from escalating regional conflict. Brent crude futures declined 85 cents, or 0.7 per cent, to $114.47 a barrel by 0720 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures were down $1.13, or 1.1 per cent, at $101.65. Brent rose 1.3 per cent and WTI gained 3 per cent on Wednesday. US Vice President JD Vance sought to revive peace negotiations by sending a letter to Iranian Security Council chief Mohsen Rezaei, the Wall Street Journal said on Wednesday, citing US officials and people familiar with the matter.

"Selling pressure is prevailing amid expectations that peace talks may resume," said Yuki Takashima, an economist at Nomura Securities. "However, the decline remains limited." This was due to concerns over intensified attacks by the Houthis and fears the US may launch an attack on Iran following its midterm elections set for November 3. The Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis said it destroyed a ballistic missile fired by the group towards the kingdom's eastern region early on Thursday, as hostilities between the two sides show no signs of abating. The Houthis attacked Aden airport on Wednesday, Yemeni government forces said. The attack came a day after the Houthis said they hit Saudi Arabia's biggest oil refinery with a missile, stepping up strikes against the world's second-largest crude producer after the United States. Saudi authorities did not immediately confirm the strike on the 550,000-barrel-per-day facility. Qatari mediators have presented Iran with a new draft deal to end the war with the US and Israel, an official briefed on the negotiations said, but a senior Iranian official dismissed it as unacceptable ideas that did not amount to an offer. Iran's foreign minister said on Wednesday Tehran continued to give diplomacy a chance to succeed and flagged the possibility of completing its seven-day plan in less than a week if adopted. Some expectations of rising crude and diesel production from Russia weighed further on market sentiment and prices. "Since the October 15 strike on the Ryazan refinery, there have been no further confirmed attacks on Russian refining infrastructure," JPMorgan analysts said in a note last night. "The silence has allowed Russian refinery runs to rebound by 350 kbd last week to 4 mbd." "Higher runs would also allow Russia to lift crude production by a broadly comparable amount, reversing part of the recent decline that pushed output to 8.4 mbd—its lowest level since 2003 ... (but) higher crude production would not necessarily translate into higher crude exports." The US Energy Information Administration said on Wednesday that energy firms pulled 1.9 million barrels of crude from storage during the week ended October 23, versus analysts' forecast of a 15,000-barrel build in a Reuters poll. But gasoline stockpiles rose by 3.9 million barrels, against analysts' expectations for a draw of 0.9 million barrels.

Source: Reuters
